hyp-1.note: title: 'CSMD1 loss relieves inhibition on C4A/C4B-mediated complement activation, leading to excessive synaptic pruning in schizophrenia', so CSMD1 is neg and C4A, C4B pos; the chain is a fan-in of three genes onto complement activation

hyp-2.note: the title names no disease; the mechanism ('Overactivity of this C1QA-C4A-CX3CR1 axis ... driving schizophrenia pathogenesis') and the chain end at schizophrenia, and give all three genes a positive sign

findings.detail: every arm of both hypotheses ends with 'synapse pruning leads to schizophrenia', and neither citation states it: PMID:26814963 ties complement activity, not pruning, to schizophrenia and offers synapse elimination only as a possible explanation of reduced synapse numbers; PMID:42276261 says 'aberrant' pruning, with no direction.

PMID:26814963 states the C4A-schizophrenia link directly ('each common C4 allele associating with schizophrenia in proportion to its tendency to generate greater expression of C4A'), and PMID:42276261 reports C4 overexpression in schizophrenia brain, but no step of either hypothesis says C4A (or C4) goes with schizophrenia; the run cites the strongest source for the steps it does not support and routes C4A through the unsupported pruning step instead; under the bridge rule (only when an arm cannot compose) BioLean has no place to put it either.

P49238 (UniProt CX3CR1), cited for 'CX3CR1 activates microglia', says CX3CR1 is 'Required to restrain the microglial inflammatory response in the CNS' (By similarity); kept as refuting, judging microglial inflammatory response and microglial activation the same node.

contradicting_evidence is empty, yet the run's own CX3CR1 citations cut against 'CX3CR1 overactivity drives schizophrenia': P49238 has CX3CR1 restraining microglial inflammation, and PMID:42276261 calls CX3CR1 the microglial counter-receptor of a 'don't eat me' signal and reports it underexpressed in schizophrenia blood (sex-specific in brain).

the only specific citation for 'C4B activates complement activation' is a GWAS Catalog row for rs116633139, an intergenic SNP near HLA-DQB1, trait 'autism spectrum disorder or schizophrenia', risk allele '?', with C4A and C4B among about 70 author-reported MHC genes; no cited text supports any C4B step, so the C4B arm has no evidence at its first step.
OT:CSMD1-MONDO_0005090 is a CSMD1-schizophrenia association score, cited for 'CSMD1 inhibits complement activation'.

PMID:26814963, cited for 'C4A activates complement activation', reports C4A expression tracking schizophrenia risk and C4 mediating synapse elimination in mice; it never says C4A activates complement (only that the results 'implicate excessive complement activity').

STRING enrichments of the run's own input genes (GO:0006958 for C1QA, C4A, C4B; GO:0098883 for CX3CR1 and C1QA, 2 of 11) are cited as evidence for causal steps; an enrichment of the query set is circular and states no step.

hyp-1 is written as a chain but is a fan-in: hyp-1.1, hyp-1.2 and hyp-1.3 each end at complement activation, and hyp-1.2 and hyp-1.3 start at C4A and C4B rather than at the previous step's object; read as a graph it connects each gene to schizophrenia.

hyp-2 has two fan-ins: hyp-2.2 starts at C4A after hyp-2.1 ends at complement activation, and hyp-2.4 starts at CX3CR1 after hyp-2.3 ends at synapse pruning; read as a graph it connects each gene to schizophrenia.
the mechanism says uninhibited complement activation drives 'the deposition of C4A and C4B' (complement to C4), while the chain says C4A and C4B activate complement (C4 to complement).

CX3CR1's role shifts across the hypothesis: a marker in the title ('CX3CR1-expressing microglia'), an undirected regulator in the mechanism ('a process regulated by the microglial receptor CX3CR1'), and an activator in the chain (hyp-2.4); the claim takes pos from the chain and 'Overactivity of this C1QA-C4A-CX3CR1 axis'.

the run leaves the CURIE empty for complement activation, synapse pruning, microglia and the brain context, and grounding_evidence is empty for every node, though it cites STRING records naming GO:0006958 and GO:0098883.

an effect on a cell type ('CX3CR1 activates microglia'): Target has no cell-type kind, so the run's 'microglia' node (object of hyp-2.4, subject of hyp-2.5) is grounded as GO:0001774 microglial cell activation, following the run's falsification text ('preventing microglial activation halts excessive synaptic pruning'); the hyp-2.5 texts name microglia, not their activation, so S8 says slightly more than its quotes.
the PMID:22632727 abstract never names its species; taxon mouse is set from the paper itself (postnatal retinogeniculate pruning with CR3/C3 disruption), not from the quoted text.
the CSMD1 and C1QA texts speak of the classical pathway (GO:0006958); the statements use the run's 'complement activation' (GO:0006956), the parent, so the evidence is for a part of the node.

the run abstains on NXPH3 and CCDC136 citing GWAS:NXPH3:no-association, GWAS:CCDC136:no-association and OT:NXPH3-MONDO_0005090, none of which is in sources.json, and claims zero Open Targets scores for both genes while citing only NXPH3's; the abstention cannot be checked.

PMID:26814963 states a direct in vivo C4-to-pruning result ('In mice, C4 mediated synapse elimination during postnatal development'), but neither hypothesis has a C4A (or C4B) to synapse pruning step; the run cites the paper only for C4A activating complement and for pruning causing schizophrenia, neither of which it states.

hyp-1's mechanism calls excessive pruning 'characteristic of schizophrenia' (a feature), and its cited PMID:26814963 offers synapse elimination only as an explanation of 'the reduced numbers of synapses in the brains of individuals with schizophrenia' (a feature), yet the chain step makes pruning a cause (synapse pruning leads_to schizophrenia).
